properties.decision:
Recorded as brainstorming on 2026-09-19 from flo2's F12, not as a proposal.

THE OBSERVATION. `set_decision_status` takes the id, the status, the approver and the date, and nothing else. It moved two decisions to `accepted` correctly and left both NAMED 'OPEN — is … the one thing flo2 is missing?' with bodies ending 'Options, none chosen.' Their sentence is the argument: 'An accepted Decision that still reads as an open question is worse than an unsettled one, because a later reader trusts the prose over the status field.'

WHY THE EXISTING ROUTE DOES NOT APPLY. `collapse_decision` is the tool for naming a winner and it needs REGISTERED alternatives; these options were prose paragraphs inside the decision text, which is what the brainstorm skill asks for. So the only route left is re-sending the whole node through add_decision with the name and body rewritten — a four-kilobyte upsert to change a status and a heading, and the exact operation measured to lose content elsewhere in the same report.

THE OPTIONS.
(a) A free-text `chose` or `outcome` on set_decision_status: the settling act says what it settled, beside the status it sets, without touching the deliberation. Smallest, and it adds a field to a setter rather than a concept to the model.
(b) Lean on `replace_text` (v0.65.0) instead: settle, then replace the 'OPEN —' heading in one call. Costs nothing to build and is available today; COUNTER — it is two acts where the user performed one, and nothing ties the new heading to the settlement.
(c) Make collapse_decision work over prose options by registering them at settle time. Largest, and it argues the options should have been alternatives all along.

⚠️ THREE ENTRIES IN THAT FILE PUSH TOWARD THE SAME DANGEROUS OPERATION — this one, the append request, and the absence of an epoch-free snapshot — and it is the one operation with no guard on it.
properties.name: OPEN — should settling a Decision be able to say WHICH option won, without rewriting the deliberation that produced it?
